items.signal_prefix: LOAD-GROWTH VIEW UPDATED: annual load growth of at least

set.signal: LOAD-GROWTH VIEW (CEO Jim Burke): annual load growth of at least 4-6% in ERCOT and 2-3% in PJM through 2030 remain reasonable estimates. NEW ALL-TIME SUMMER PEAKS set in July 2026 — PJM over 168 GW and ERCOT over 91 GW — and the grids met them, which Vistra argues disproves the claim that these markets cannot handle the load growth. Data centers matter 'particularly in 2028 and beyond', but a significant part of the growth is industrial reshoring, electrification, Texas population growth and broader economic expansion: of the ~5-6% ERCOT CAGR, ~3% is non-data-center (oil & gas, residential, small business) and ~2% is data centers.

items.reason: The comparison with the Q1 2026 call is not in this source; the load-growth view is the CEO's.
items.evidence: We believe annual load growth of at least 4%-6% in ERCOT and 2%-3% in PJM through 2030 remain reasonable estimates for these markets.

items.label: Vistra Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)

set.signal: ERCOT QUEUE REALITY CHECK: Vistra's May-2024 forecast of 115-120 GW of ERCOT load in 2030 is UNCHANGED despite the queue growing to what has at times been expressed as OVER 400 GW — Vistra thinks the real data-center number is 12-15 GW by 2030, i.e. the queue overstates demand by MORE THAN 20x. Governor Abbott's directive triggers a data-center audit that will likely pause ERCOT/PUC reviews for 'a couple of months'; CEO: Vistra was 'expecting to hear where we would stand from a base load for Batch Zero any day now. We expect that's going to get kicked out'. Vistra supports thinning the queue. Its Comanche Peak project targets energization at END OF 2027 and is not seen as affected; Vistra has projects in Batch Zero baseload, Batch Zero to-be-studied load and the coming Batch One. CEO: 'It is possible that there were people looking to energize here in the more short-term horizon that might see a delay.'

items.reason: Hedges restored: the CEO said a delay for near-term energizations 'is possible', and that the Batch Zero result is expected to be 'kicked out'.
items.evidence: It is possible that there were people looking to energize here in the more short-term horizon that might see a delay.

items.signal_prefix: NEW-BUILD ECONOMICS GAP: ERCOT year-to-date wholesale power

set.signal: NEW-BUILD ECONOMICS GAP: ERCOT year-to-date wholesale power has been $30/MWh (same as last year) — CEO: '30 is not going to get new stuff built.' The price of generation EQUIPMENT 'has doubled, if not tripled' in some cases, so what was an acceptable build price a year or two ago no longer is. In PJM the $555/MW-day RBP cap 'might get some things built' but a spread around it will be needed for certain projects. Large-load customers are willing to contract with EXISTING assets at a PREMIUM because it is still a discount to new build; co-location can beat even an islanded new build on speed.

items.label: Vistra Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)

set.signal: ERCOT SCARCITY-PRICING MECHANICS (Head of Commercial): on July 22, 2026 a ~3.5-hour window as solar dropped off required ~25 GWh of battery discharge against only ~31 GWh available on the system, yet the day cleared just $57/MWh because batteries, knowing they would not run out, chased the bottom to deplete energy — 'very easy that that day could have cleared in closer to a $400 or $500 day.' CEO: battery returns since the large post-August-2023 ECRS payments 'have been about a fifth of what investors probably expected', and battery queues are slowing. Vistra reads current ERCOT softness as recency bias plus lumpy load timing; the load it expects to hook up was always a 2027-2028 event.

items.label: Vistra Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: REGULATORY: FERC's JUNE 2026 CO-LOCATION ORDER directs PJM a

set.signal: REGULATORY: FERC's JUNE 2026 CO-LOCATION ORDER directs PJM and its transmission owners to accommodate co-location and adopt the corresponding transmission services — Stacey Doré: 'The order itself, frankly, adopted a lot of Vistra's arguments and positions'. PJM and the TOs, ordered to make a compliance filing by mid-August, have asked for more time; a filing specifying the arrangements and applicable rates is expected within roughly 30-60 days. Vistra opposes the 'bring your own new capacity' mandate contemplated in the IRAS proposal (a 'stick' approach that could require large loads to curtail ahead of those PAID to curtail) and favors incentives for data-center flexibility; it argues IRAS may actually push customers FURTHER toward co-location with existing resources, since co-location avoids transmission build and customers bring backup generation anyway. Customer appetite in PJM remains for BOTH energy and capacity, not energy-only.

items.reason: Quote made verbatim: the source has 'frankly,' inside the quoted sentence, spoken by Stacey Doré.
items.evidence: The order itself, frankly, adopted a lot of Vistra's arguments and positions as we advocated for those projects to be available to customers.
